findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the internet-facing portal instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host unrestricted outbound channels for data exfiltration or command-and-control. Combined with the cleartext HTTP (port 80) listener open to the world, the host has no network boundary in either direction.

The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

No metadata_options block is configured, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled on an internet-facing instance, allowing SSRF-style attacks to read instance metadata including the credentials embedded in user data.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root volume (which also contains the user_data-derived secrets) is created without EBS encryption at rest unless account-level default encryption is enabled.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, placing the host directly on the public internet with no load balancer or bastion boundary, and combined with open SSH it forms a directly reachable attack surface holding hard-coded credentials.
The EBS data volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data is stored unencrypted on disk.

The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), so network telemetry is stored without an explicitly enforced encryption policy.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the flow log bucket, so nothing prevents a future ACL or bucket policy from exposing network metadata publicly; protection relies entirely on account defaults.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, so flow log objects containing network metadata may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP automatically, defeating network segmentation and expanding external attack surface by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP automatically, defeating network segmentation and expanding external attack surface by default.

force_destroy = true on the VPC flow log archive bucket allows all stored network audit records to be deleted along with the bucket by a single terraform destroy, undermining the integrity and availability of security log evidence.
